questions.question: A team is designing a low-cost water filter for a school demonstration. Which statement is a design criterion?
choices: The team has two class periods to build it
The filter must reduce visible sediment by at least 80%
The team has $15 to spend
Only materials in the classroom may be used

questions.question: A design constraint differs from a criterion because a constraint
choices: describes a feature that makes the solution successful
is the final test result
sets a limit the design must work within
is a drawing of the prototype

questions.question: Why do engineers build a prototype before producing a final device?
choices: To avoid needing to test the design
To prove the first idea is always correct
To remove all constraints from the problem
To examine how a design works and find changes to make

questions.question: Two bridge models use the same materials. One holds more mass but takes longer to assemble. What does this comparison illustrate?
choices: A trade-off between performance and assembly time
A controlled variable that should be ignored
A result that proves one model is unsafe
A criterion that cannot be measured

questions.question: A group changes the wing shape and also changes the launch angle between trials. What is the main problem?
choices: The model uses too few materials
The test does not isolate the effect of wing shape
The group has already optimized its design
The launch angle is a dependent variable

questions.question: A prototype repeatedly tips over when a load is placed near one edge. Which revision is most directly supported by this evidence?
choices: Add decoration to the upper frame
Increase the load during every later trial
Make the base wider or lower the center of mass
Remove the measurement scale

questions.question: Which sequence best represents an iterative engineering process?
choices: Build once, present, then avoid changes
Choose materials, advertise, and skip evaluation
Test a final product before identifying criteria
Define a need, design, build, test, and revise

questions.question: A team tests three insulation materials around identical cups of warm water. Which variable should be kept constant for a fair comparison?
choices: The type of thermometer used in every cup
The temperature change measured after ten minutes
The insulation material around each cup
The conclusion the team hopes to reach

questions.question: A water-rocket team wants to compare how fin area affects flight distance. Which design best tests that question?
choices: Change fin area, pressure, and mass together
Change fin area while holding launch pressure and rocket mass as constant as possible
Use a different launch surface for each fin size
Measure only the longest flight and discard the rest

questions.question: A team's first solar oven reaches 48°C, below its 60°C target. What is the best next step?
choices: Claim that the oven meets the criterion because it became warm
Change several features and skip another measurement
Record the result, inspect heat-loss paths, and test a targeted revision
Replace the target with the measured result

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a project specification?
choices: To guarantee the prototype will work on the first attempt
To replace all testing with a written plan
To record only the names of team members
To list the problem, measurable success criteria, and important constraints

questions.question: A team has limited battery capacity and must choose between a faster motor and a longer operating time. This is best described as
choices: a trade-off between competing design goals
a random error in measurement
a failure to define the problem
a controlled experiment with no variables

questions.question: A ramp design moves a cart farther, but it also makes the cart harder to stop safely. Which action shows responsible design reasoning?
choices: Keep the longer ramp because distance is the only useful criterion
Compare both performance goals and test a safe stopping feature
Remove the stopping test because it complicates the project
Change the safety criterion after each trial

questions.question: Why should a team repeat a prototype test several times?
choices: One test always identifies every source of error
Repeated tests guarantee the design meets all criteria
Repeated tests help reveal variability and make comparisons more dependable
More tests make measurement methods unnecessary

questions.question: A sensor's readings jump between 18 and 19 units when the environment is steady. What is a sensible first response?
choices: Assume the largest reading is the true value
Delete every reading that differs from the expected result
Replace the sensor with an unrelated actuator
Check the sensor setup and collect repeated readings before changing the design

questions.question: Which change would most likely improve the reliability of a small wind-turbine test?
choices: Use the same fan distance and speed for each blade design
Move the fan closer whenever a turbine performs poorly
Change both blade shape and generator between trials
Record only whether the turbine spins

questions.question: A team selects a material because it is strong, lightweight, and recyclable, but it exceeds the budget. Which decision best addresses the full design problem?
choices: Ignore cost because strength is measurable
Compare alternative materials against all criteria and the cost constraint
Remove recyclability from the results without review
Choose the strongest material automatically

questions.question: An engineer uses a scale model of a flood barrier. Why should the team be cautious when applying model results to a full-size river?
choices: Scale models cannot represent any real structure
A smaller model has no measurable variables
Some forces and conditions may not scale proportionally
The full-size barrier will have identical water flow by definition

questions.question: Which evidence would best support the claim that a redesigned package protects its contents better?
choices: A drawing showing the new package is larger
A statement that the team prefers the new color
One successful drop of the redesigned package
Repeated drop-test damage scores for the old and new designs under the same conditions

questions.question: A project works in a classroom trial but fails outdoors in cold weather. What should the team do next?
choices: Revise the test conditions to include realistic temperature ranges and evaluate changes
Conclude the device cannot be improved
Report only the classroom result as universal evidence
Remove temperature from the design requirements
